stories.headline: Voters back data center curbs in 29+ US localities; Texas elects a moratorium-backing governor

key_facts.fact: Voters in at least 29 US jurisdictions passed bans or restrictions on data centers on Tuesday, Nov. 3, per The Washington Post.
key_facts.excerpt: Voters in at least 29 jurisdictions across the country passed bans or restrictions on data centers Tuesday, reflecting the widespread public revulsion to the facilities

key_facts.fact: Counts still differ as returns come in: the tracker Data Centers on the Ballot shows restrictions passing or leading in at least 33 communities with one pro-construction win, in North Dakota; Ballotpedia listed 41 local measures across 10 states.
key_facts.excerpt: Voters in at least 33 US communities backed restrictions on data centres... Only one local measure, in North Dakota, went the way of those supporting construction, according to the tracker Data Centers on the Ballot... Nationally, Ballotpedia listed 41 local data centre measures across 10 states.

key_facts.fact: Democrat Gina Hinojosa beat Texas Gov. Greg Abbott after pledging a moratorium on new data center construction; the AP called the race at 11:17 p.m. ET, and Texas accounts for more than 25% of planned US capacity by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: The Associated Press declared Hinojosa the winner at 11:17 p.m. ET. Hinojosa, Texas' first Latina governor, has pledged to impose a moratorium on data center construction in Texas, which accounts for more than 25% of planned US capacity by 2030.

key_facts.fact: Jefferies estimated Hinojosa's proposed moratorium could put 13.3 GW of announced Texas projects at risk, Fast Company reports, citing The Wall Street Journal.
key_facts.excerpt: Jefferies estimated that Hinojosa's proposed moratorium could put 13.3 gigawatts of announced Texas data center projects at risk, potentially delaying construction or forcing developers to abandon their plans.

key_facts.fact: Texas accounts for 41% of new US data center capacity in 2028 per SemiAnalysis; Democrats also won the next three states for new capacity (Ohio, Georgia, Arizona), and nearly two-thirds of 2028 capacity could face delays, Axios reports.
key_facts.excerpt: Texas, which accounts for 41% of new U.S. capacity in 2028, according to the research firm SemiAnalysis. Democrats won all three of the states that follow Texas for new data center capacity, including Ohio, Georgia and Arizona... nearly two-thirds of 2028 data center capacity could face delays

key_facts.fact: Trenton, Ohio voters passed a ban on data centers above 25 MW with 80% of the vote, blocking the city's plan to annex about 600 acres for a 1,000 MW Amazon campus; the AWS project could still proceed if the land stays in surrounding townships.
key_facts.excerpt: Trenton, Ohio voters passed a ban on data centres above 25MW with 80% of the vote... The ban blocks the city's plan to annex around 600 acres for a 1,000MW Amazon data centre campus. Because it applies only within city limits, the AWS project could still proceed if the land stays in the surrounding townships

key_facts.fact: AI stocks came under pressure overnight; Wells Fargo puts 27% of planned data center gigawatts in Texas, Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives called the Texas result the biggest worry of the night for the AI trade, and CNBC notes SpaceX is building multiple gigawatts of capacity, including in Texas.
key_facts.excerpt: Artificial intelligence stocks came under pressure overnight... SpaceX is currently building out multiple gigawatts of data center capacity, including projects in Texas... He added that the election in Texas was the "biggest worry" of the night for tech investors and the AI trade... According to Wells Fargo, 27% of planned data center gigawatts is in the Lone Star State.

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk responded on X: 'Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now.'
key_facts.excerpt: Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now

stories.headline: FT: Oracle scraps $7B lease of 100,000 AI chips to Tencent after Trump administration pressure

key_facts.fact: Oracle has canceled a chip-leasing contract with Tencent after pressure from the Trump administration, the Financial Times reported on Nov. 4, citing people familiar with the matter.
key_facts.excerpt: Oracle has canceled a multibillion-dollar chip leasing contract with Tencent after bowing to pressure from the Trump administration, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: The deal, worth an estimated $7B and Tencent's largest overseas lease, was a five-year agreement across multiple Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia giving access to about 100,000 advanced AI chips not available in China.
key_facts.excerpt: Tencent signed its largest overseas lease deal, worth an estimated US$7 billion, with Oracle... access to about 100,000 advanced artificial intelligence chips that were not available in China... a five-year lease across multiple Oracle data centres in South-east Asia

key_facts.fact: Pressure came from both sides: US officials raised concerns with Oracle, while top officials in Guangdong, where Tencent is based, visited the company and asked it to support domestic Chinese chips.
key_facts.excerpt: US officials approached Oracle to raise concerns about the Tencent deal... Tencent also received visits from top officials in Guangdong, where the group is based, who asked the company to support domestic Chinese chips

key_facts.fact: Overseas chip-leasing deals of this kind are currently allowed under existing rules, though US companies face increasing pressure to limit business with Chinese customers.
key_facts.excerpt: Although such overseas leasing deals are currently allowed under existing rules, US companies are facing increasing pressure to limit their business with Chinese customers.

key_facts.fact: Reuters could not immediately verify the report; Oracle, Tencent and the White House did not respond to its requests for comment.
key_facts.excerpt: Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Oracle, Tencent and the White House did not respond to Reuters requests for comment on the report

stories.headline: Bloomberg: Chinese firms ordered 6M Nvidia RTX Pro 5500s worth $70B, expect ~1% within four months

key_facts.fact: Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and other Chinese AI and cloud firms have ordered about 6 million RTX Pro 5500 chips in total, but expect only some tens of thousands, roughly 1%, within the next four months, according to people familiar with the matter.
key_facts.excerpt: have in total ordered about 6 million of Nvidia's RTX Pro 5500 chips, according to people familiar with the matter. Yet the companies predict they will get only some tens of thousands, or roughly 1%, within the next four months

key_facts.fact: The orders are worth about $70B at more than $11,000 per chip, and the RTX Pro 5500 is not subject to the US ban on selling Nvidia's most advanced chips to China.
key_facts.excerpt: Although the US has prohibited Nvidia from selling its most advanced chips to China, the RTX Pro 5500 is not subject to restrictions. Sources said that the total value of orders so far is about USD70 billion based on a unit price of more than USD11,000 per chip.

key_facts.fact: Chinese developers expect a first batch of several thousand chips before the end of 2026 and tens of thousands more around February 2027; hyperscalers estimate about 700,000 by the end of 2027, though Nvidia warned capacity will stay limited.
key_facts.excerpt: first batch of several thousand RTX Pro 5500 chips to be delivered before the end of 2026, followed by another batch of tens of thousands around February 2027... may receive about 700,000 RTX Pro 5500 chips by the end of 2027... Nvidia warned customers that capacity will remain limited for the foreseeable future

key_facts.fact: With insufficient global production capacity, Nvidia is prioritizing companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: with insufficient global production capacity, Nvidia is prioritizing companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic

key_facts.fact: Earlier reports had put the orders at over 3 million units and $35B; the new figure roughly doubles both. The chip has the same CUDA cores as the RTX 5090 with 84GB of GDDR7 memory.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese firms were suggested to have spent $35 billion on orders for over 3 million of the GPUs... The RTX Pro 5500 has the same CUDA cores as its flagship gaming GPU, the RTX 5090, but with a boosted 84GB GDDR7 memory count

stories.headline: AMD Q3 revenue rises 45% to $13.4B; $17B Q4 guide would top Intel's revenue for the first time

key_facts.fact: AMD reported Q3 revenue of $13.38B against $13.09B expected and adjusted EPS of $2.09 against $1.95; shares rose 8% in extended trading.
key_facts.excerpt: Earnings per share: $2.09 adjusted vs. $1.95 expected. Revenue: $13.38 billion vs. $13.09 billion expected... The stock jumped 8% in extended trading.

key_facts.fact: Data Center revenue hit a record $8.5B, up 97% year over year, driven by EPYC CPUs and the launch of Instinct MI450 Series GPUs; client and gaming revenue fell 8% to $3.7B, with gaming down 40%.
key_facts.excerpt: Data Center segment revenue was a record $8.5 billion, up 97% year-over-year... Client and Gaming segment revenue was $3.7 billion, down 8% year-over-year... Gaming business revenue was $773 million, down 40% year-over-year

key_facts.fact: AMD guided Q4 revenue to about $17B, plus or minus 3%, implying 66% year-over-year growth, versus a $16.2B analyst average.
key_facts.excerpt: For the fourth quarter, AMD said it expects about $17 billion in revenue, beating the $16.2 billion average analyst estimate, according to LSEG.

key_facts.fact: Intel expects $15B to $16B for the same quarter, so hitting its guidance would put AMD's quarterly sales above Intel's for the first time, by about $1.5B at the midpoints.
key_facts.excerpt: If AMD meets its guidance, its quarterly sales will surpass those of its considerably bigger rival Intel for the first time in history... its projected advantage will be approximately $1.5 billion at the midpoint of both companies' forecasts

key_facts.fact: Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure are running models and workloads on the first Helios rack-scale systems, AMD's rival to Nvidia's Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD also sells data center GPUs and full rack-scale systems called Helios that compete directly with Nvidia's Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems. Meta, Microsoft, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Oracle are all beginning to use AMD Helios in their data centers.

key_facts.fact: For 2027, AMD now expects server revenue to double and Data Center to exceed 80% of total revenue, up from 64% in Q3; it expects Data Center to grow about 50% sequentially in Q4.
key_facts.excerpt: We now expect server revenue to double year over year in 2027... we expect Data Center to be more than 80% of our total revenue in 2027... a sharp increase in our Data Center segment of approximately 50% growth

stories.headline: Super Micro lifts FY2027 sales forecast to $72-82B after record $19.9B quarter; margin slips

key_facts.fact: Super Micro reported record fiscal Q1 net sales of $19.9B, versus $11.1B in the prior quarter and $5.0B a year earlier; net income was $1,594M against $168M a year earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: Net sales of $19.9 billion versus $11.1 billion in Q4'26 and $5.0 billion in Q1'26... Net income of $1,594 million versus $1,178 million in Q4'26 and $168 million in Q1'26.

key_facts.fact: Revenue of $19.95B beat the $16.39B LSEG average, and adjusted EPS of $1.81 beat $1.23 estimates, though the company had already issued preliminary results above guidance in October.
key_facts.excerpt: First-quarter revenue totaled $19.95 billion, against an average analyst estimate of $16.39 billion... Adjusted earnings were $1.81 per share... versus estimates of $1.23... The company had issued preliminary first-quarter results that exceeded its earlier guidance

key_facts.fact: The new information is the outlook: fiscal Q2 revenue of $19.5B to $21.5B against a $17.14B estimate, and fiscal 2027 revenue of $72B to $82B, up from a prior $65B to $72B.
key_facts.excerpt: projected second-quarter revenue between $19.5 billion and $21.5 billion, compared with an analyst estimate of $17.14 billion... fiscal 2027 revenue forecast of $72.0 billion to $82.0 billion. Its prior forecast was $65.0 billion to $72.0 billion

key_facts.fact: Gross margin was 12.7%, down from 17.5% in the prior quarter but up from 9.3% a year earlier, and operations used $434M of cash.
key_facts.excerpt: Gross margin of 12.7% versus 17.5% in Q4'26 and 9.3% in Q1'26... Cash flow used in operations for Q1'27 of $434 million

key_facts.fact: Super Micro appointed former Western Digital executive Mark Long as CFO last month, nearly two years after launching a search amid concerns over its financial and accounting practices.
key_facts.excerpt: Super Micro Computer appointed former Western Digital executive Mark Long as CFO last month, nearly two years after launching a search for the role amid concerns over its financial and accounting practices

stories.headline: Google to invest $15B in Malaysia in 2027-28 for data center campuses and over 1 GW of clean energy

key_facts.fact: Google said on Nov. 4 it will invest $15B in Malaysia from 2027 to 2028, going toward data center campuses, clean energy, water security and upskilling workers.
key_facts.excerpt: Google will invest $15 billion in Malaysia from 2027 to 2028 with the spending going towards data centre campuses, clean energy, bolstering water security and upskilling workers

key_facts.fact: Alphabet president and chief investment officer Ruth Porat announced the plan at an event at Universiti Malaya with Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
key_facts.excerpt: Ruth Porat, the president and chief investment officer of Alphabet and its subsidiary, Google LLC, announced this at an event at Universiti Malaya today with Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.

key_facts.fact: New campuses are planned in Selangor and Negeri Sembilan, in addition to the operational campus at Elmina Business Park in Selangor.
key_facts.excerpt: Google plans to build new campuses in the states of Selangor and Negeri Sembilan, in addition to its first campus at Elmina Business Park in Selangor, which is already operational.

key_facts.fact: Google plans to add more than 1 GW of clean energy capacity to the grid, anchored by a collaboration with utility Tenaga Nasional Berhad, under what Porat called a 'bring your own power' approach.
key_facts.excerpt: Describing it as "BYOP" or "bring your own power", she said this investment will add more than one gigawatt of clean energy capacity to Malaysia's grid... Anchored by a new strategic collaboration with Tenaga Nasional Berhad

key_facts.fact: Google says it will pay for 100% of the power its campuses use and the direct grid-connection costs, with campuses running at a Power Usage Effectiveness of 1.12 to 1.14.
key_facts.excerpt: Google will also pay for 100 per cent of the power its data centre campuses use and the direct infrastructure costs required to connect them to the grid... its Malaysian campuses will run at a Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of 1.12 to 1.14.

key_facts.fact: The pledge expands on a $2B investment announced in 2024; Malaysia accounts for more than half of under-construction data center capacity among Southeast Asian peers, per DC Byte, and data centers are forecast to take one-third of its energy by 2035.
key_facts.excerpt: expanding on a $2 billion investment announced in 2024... Malaysia accounts for more than half of under-construction Data centre capacity among Southeast Asian countries... by 2035, Data centres are forecast to swallow up one-third of Malaysia's total energy consumption
